Build reports for listed datasets

Source: R/reports.R
dataset_report.Rd

Builds a detailed report for every dataset with a unique dataset_id, based on a Quarto (.qmd) template. The reports are rendered as html files and saved in the specified output folder.

dataset_report(
  dataset_id,
  database,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  output_path = "export/reports",
  input_file = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE,
  keep = FALSE,
  show_questions = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset_id

Name of specific study/dataset

database

A compiled database

overwrite

Logical value to determine whether to overwrite existing report

output_path

Location where rendered report will be saved

input_file

Report template (.qmd) to build the study report from. The default, NULL, uses config/report_dataset.qmd if the working directory has one, and otherwise the generic template shipped with traits.build (see the Report template section). A path given here is always used.

quiet

An option to suppress printing during rendering from knitr, Quarto and pandoc

keep

Keep the temporary, per-dataset copy of the template (see the Report template section)?

show_questions

Include the questions to the data contributor? The default, TRUE, gives the review copy; FALSE gives a final copy with all questions (and the explanatory text about them) omitted.

Value

Invisibly, a logical named by dataset_id, TRUE where the report was written. Reports are rendered as html files in output_path. A dataset whose report fails to render warns and returns FALSE rather than aborting the batch.

Details

Run this from the root of the database's repository: the report reads each dataset's data/<dataset_id>/metadata.yml from there.

Report template

traits.build ships a generic template, which introduces the database from its own metadata (the metadata block of config/metadata.yml: title, version, description, DOI, reference, repository and licence) and works for any database the package builds.

A database can use its own template instead by saving it as config/report_dataset.qmd, beside its other build inputs. When input_file is NULL, dataset_report() uses that file if it exists in the working directory, and otherwise the generic template. To start one, copy the generic template:

file.copy(system.file("support", "report_dataset.qmd", package = "traits.build"),
          "config/report_dataset.qmd")

A template receives the parameters dataset_id, austraits_path (the compiled database, saved as .rds) and show_questions, and must declare all three under params: in its YAML header, or rendering fails. It also needs a title: line there, which dataset_report() replaces with the dataset's id. The template is copied into the working directory and rendered from there, so any path it uses, such as an image or an included file, is relative to the working directory, not to config/. keep = TRUE leaves that copy, tmp_<dataset_id>_report.qmd, in the working directory.
